aihole.tagline: Cradle of Indian rock architecture — 120+ temples where Chalukya architects experimented

eateries.name: Badami Court Hotel Restaurant (Badami base)
eateries.area: Station Road extension, Badami (35km — Aihole has no dinner option)
eateries.why_it_matters: Aihole has no proper sit-down dinner option — most overnight visitors base in Badami (35km / 1 hour drive) and use Badami Court Hotel's mid-range AC restaurant. Listed here because it is the de-facto evening anchor for Aihole-focused archaeology/heritage tourists. Multi-cuisine menu including North Karnataka regional section + non-veg biryani (one of few non-veg options in the whole Chalukya circuit). Open 7am-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Plan Aihole as a morning-only stop (8am-1pm) and return to Badami for lunch — Aihole village offers no AC sit-down options beyond breakfast. Pre-book Badami Court dinner on weekends; archaeology survey teams fill it Sat-Sun. UPI and cards both.

eateries.name: Hotel Paradise Family Restaurant (Badami 35km base)
eateries.area: Station Road, near LIC Office, Badami (35km — Aihole has no AC sit-down dinner)
eateries.why_it_matters: Aihole has no proper sit-down dinner option after the ASI gate closes. Most overnight visitors stage in Badami (35km / 1 hour drive). Hotel Paradise on Station Road is the most consistent tandoor and multi-cuisine kitchen in Badami town, with both veg and non-veg sections — one of few non-veg options across the entire Chalukya circuit. Free parking out front; family-restaurant format with AC and à la carte service.
eateries.insider_tip: Plan Aihole as a 8:00-13:00 morning stop and drive back to Badami for late-lunch or dinner. Pre-book on weekends; archaeology survey teams and Hubballi weekenders fill it. UPI and cards both work. Gobi tikka and jolada-rotti thali are the picks.
eateries.signature_address: Station Road, near LIC Office, Badami 587201

eateries.name: Badami Heritage Resort Restaurant (Badami 35km base)
eateries.area: Inside Badami Heritage Resort, Station Road, Badami (35km — Aihole village has no formal sit-down lunch)
eateries.why_it_matters: Budget pure-veg alternative to Badami Court Hotel for archaeology visitors on the Aihole-Pattadakal-Badami circuit. Lunch is a fixed unlimited South Indian thali (₹90 — one of the best value sit-down thalis in the Chalukya triangle). No eggs, no alcohol — strict pure-veg kitchen. Open hotel restaurant; non-residents welcome. Dinner is à la carte but limited; lunch is the primary draw.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch thali 12:30-15:00 is the sweet spot — order before 13:30 to avoid the temple-tour bus crowd. Breakfast 07:30-10:00. Dinner 19:30-22:00 but à la carte only (skip if you want regional food — Hotel Paradise tandoor is better). Cash and UPI both.
eateries.signature_address: Inside Badami Heritage Resort, Station Road, Badami 587201

eateries.name: Aihole Roopali Canteen
eateries.area: Aihole village main road, opposite Durga Temple turnoff
eateries.why_it_matters: Family-run pure-veg breakfast and lunch counter on the Aihole main road — the village-level option used by ASI workers, ASI security, and the few local pilgrims arriving for Meguti Jain temple worship. Tin-roof shed with 5-6 plastic tables. Khara bath and pesarattu are the regional anchors. Open 6.30am-3pm only — no dinner service. Cash only.
eateries.insider_tip: Pre-9am for breakfast — by 10am the Pattadakal-bound tour vehicles fill the road and this small counter sells out of khara bath. The only village-level option; don't expect English signage. Bring exact cash; UPI inconsistent.

eateries.name: KSTDC Mayura Chalukya Aihole Canteen
eateries.area: Near Aihole museum, ASI complex entrance
eateries.signature_dish: KSTDC veg thali for tour groups
eateries.why_it_matters: KSTDC-run canteen attached to the Aihole museum and ASI ticket gate — the only formal food option inside Aihole village. Run on a thali-and-tiffin model: jolada roti + dal + curd + a regional vegetable curry (₹120) is the standard plate. Most tour groups eat here between the Durga Temple visit and the drive on to Pattadakal. Open 9am-6pm, closed Mondays (museum day).
eateries.insider_tip: Pre-noon lunch (11.30am-12.30pm) is quietest — by 1pm tour buses from Hubballi/Bagalkot fill it. Skip on Mondays — museum closed, canteen closed too. UPI works; cards unreliable. Carry water — no proper shop after this on the Pattadakal road.

eateries.name: Geeta Darshini (Badami 35km base)
eateries.area: Main Road, opposite Bus Stand, Badami
eateries.signature_dish: Masala dosa with sambhar and coconut chutney
eateries.why_it_matters: The Aihole-Pattadakal-Badami circuit starts at dawn — temples open 6am and Aihole has no breakfast counter. Geeta Darshini opens early on Badami's bus-stand stretch and turns around an idli-vada-dosa plate in five minutes flat, run by a Udupi family whose South-Indian menu is short and consistent. Locals outnumber tourists at the steel-tumbler counter; service is brusque and the room is tiny but the dosa batter is fermented overnight and the sambhar is properly tempered with curry leaf and asafoetida.
eateries.insider_tip: Cash only and seating is six tables — arrive before 8am if heading out to Aihole, or wait for the 10am post-rush window. Skip the limited North Indian items and stick to the South Indian board.
eateries.signature_address: Main Road, opposite Bus Stand, Badami, Bagalkot 587201

eateries.name: Golden Caves Restaurant (Badami 35km base)
eateries.signature_dish: North Karnataka thali with jolada rotti and ennegai
eateries.why_it_matters: Golden Caves is the highest-rated independent restaurant on the Badami strip and the only mid-range option that takes the North Karnataka grain belt seriously — jolada rotti (sorghum) and ennegai (stuffed brinjal in groundnut-coconut masala) on a banana leaf, not the pan-Indian buffet most hotel restaurants default to. It's a useful counterpart to the temple-circuit start: Aihole, Pattadakal and Badami Caves are all dry on lunch options and the village stalls do informal jolada rotti only.
eateries.insider_tip: The thali sells out by 2:30pm — order it on arrival and ask for extra kalu palya (greens) on the side. Non-veg menu exists but the kitchen is built for the veg combination plate.

badami.tagline: Chalukya cave temples carved from red sandstone cliffs — India's earliest Hindu rock architecture

eateries.name: Hotel Sanman Deluxe
eateries.why_it_matters: Pure-veg Badami workhorse near the bus stand and railway road — the lunch-stop for domestic pilgrims doing the Chalukya triangle (Badami-Aihole-Pattadakal). North Karnataka jolada roti (sorghum flatbread) thali is the regional anchor — served with brinjal ennegayi (stuffed eggplant), dal, jaggery, and buttermilk. Open 7am-10pm; family-run for 2+ decades.
eateries.insider_tip: Jolada-roti thali peaks 12.30-2pm — order by 1pm to avoid the temple-tour bus crowd. Cash and UPI both work. Skip the South Indian tiffin if doing the regional thali; portions are large.

eateries.name: Hotel Mookambika Deluxe
eateries.area: Station Road, near Badami bus stand
eateries.why_it_matters: Second of the two main Badami pure-veg restaurants on Station Road. Often runs in parallel with Sanman; locals split between the two by day of week. Bele holige (jaggery + chana dal stuffed flatbread) is the festival-week order. Bigger lunch hall, 80+ seats, family-table service. Open 7am-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: If Sanman is full (it usually is 1-2pm), Mookambika is the immediate fallback 100m away. Bele holige is seasonal — peaks around Diwali, Sankranti, and Banashankari Jatre (January). UPI works; cards unreliable.

eateries.name: Hotel Mayura Chalukya (KSTDC)
eateries.area: Ramdurg Road, near Badami cave temples
eateries.why_it_matters: KSTDC (Karnataka State Tourism Development Corporation) property restaurant, the only AC mid-range option within walking distance of the cave-temple ASI gate. Buffet lunch for group tours (₹400 fixed) plus à la carte vegetarian and limited non-veg menu. Used by ASI guides as the standard lunch stop after morning cave-temple visits. Open 7am-10pm.
eateries.insider_tip: If staying in town, the buffet lunch is the easiest mid-range option after the morning cave walk. Pre-book for groups of 6+; weekend lunch fills 1-2pm with TN/AP tour buses. Cards and UPI both work — the KSTDC desk is set up for tourists.

eateries.name: Geeta Darshan
eateries.why_it_matters: Local pure-veg tiffin counter on the Badami main road — used by railway-station arrivals for breakfast before the 8am Chalukya circuit start. Khara bath (savoury upma with semolina + vegetables) and pesarattu (green-gram dosa) are the regional anchors not always on Sanman/Mookambika menus. Open 6.30am-9pm; busy 7-9am.
eateries.insider_tip: Pre-7.30am for breakfast before the 8am ASI-cave gate opening. Khara bath with chow-chow bath (sweet + savoury semolina pair) is the local breakfast convention. Cash preferred; small UPI display behind counter.

eateries.name: Restaurant at Badami Court Hotel
eateries.area: Station Road extension, near Badami camp layout
eateries.signature_dish: Multi-cuisine buffet with North Karnataka section
eateries.why_it_matters: AC hotel restaurant inside the Badami Court Hotel (mid-range business hotel used by archaeologists and overnight tour groups). Multi-cuisine menu with a North Karnataka section (jolada roti + ennegayi + bele holige), plus non-veg biryani — one of the few sit-down non-veg options in Badami. Open 7am-10.30pm; pool-side lunch on weekends.
eateries.insider_tip: The only AC + non-veg option in town. Pre-book lunch on weekends — fills with archaeology survey teams and ASI tour groups Sat-Sun. Mutton biryani is the non-veg call; veg pulao is reliably good. Cards and UPI both.

bandipur.tagline: Nilgiri Biosphere tiger reserve — elephants, leopards, and India's most scenic safari road

eateries.name: JLR Bandipur Safari Lodge Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Jungle Lodges and Resorts (JLR Karnataka — KSTDC-affiliated wildlife properties) operates Bandipur Safari Lodge at Melukamanahalli, on the reserve edge — restaurant open to non-residents for lunch + dinner with prior booking. Set Karnataka thali with safari-package timing 1-2.30pm + 8-10pm. Open 7am-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch booking essential — 10-15 outside-guest covers per service. Set menu fixed; ₹650-850 per person. Cards, UPI, cash all work. Lodge dining hall has wildlife-photo wall + naturalist briefing pre-safari.

eateries.name: Country Club Tusker Trails Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Country Club Tusker Trails is a multi-amenity resort at Mangala village, 8km from Bandipur Reception — restaurant open to non-residents for lunch and dinner, buffet model. Pool-side seating; non-resident pool access ₹500 extra. Open 7am-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch buffet 1-3pm ₹650 veg / ₹850 non-veg. Dinner 7.30-10pm a la carte. Card, UPI, cash all work. Adjacent to NH-181 — lunch stop for Mysore-Ooty road travellers.

eateries.name: Hotel Vinod Bar Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Hotel Vinod is a Gundlupet town-side highway restaurant on NH-181 — the gateway-town stop 25km from Bandipur Reception, common lunch break for Bengaluru-Ooty/Mysore-Wayanad travellers. Karnataka mutton biryani is the call. Open 7am-11pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch 12.30-3pm; biryani fresh-batch 1pm and 2pm. Truck-driver clientele early morning; tourist crowd lunch. Cash and UPI; card sometimes works. Highway-side parking ample.

eateries.name: Mayura Prakruti KSTDC
eateries.why_it_matters: Mayura Prakruti (KSTDC Karnataka Tourism property) is the only government-run dining option at Bandipur Reception — open to walk-in non-residents for breakfast/lunch/dinner. Karnataka veg meals ₹220. Pre-safari breakfast 7-9am the default for safari-bookers. Open 7am-10pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Breakfast 7-9am before morning safari; arrive 6.45am for first batch. Lunch 12.30-3pm. Cards, UPI, cash all work. Adjacent to Bandipur Tourist Reception Centre — safari booking + Mayura combined breakfast is the standard sequence.
eateries.signature_address: KSTDC Mayura Prakruti, Bandipur Reception, NH-181, Bandipur 571126

eateries.name: Tusker Trails Cafe
eateries.why_it_matters: Tusker Trails Cafe is a small NH-181 highway cafe (opened ~2018, 4km N of Bandipur Reception) — common safari-day morning coffee + post-safari afternoon stop. Filter coffee from Coorg + Chikmagalur estate supply. Open 7am-7pm; closed Tuesdays.
eateries.insider_tip: Post-safari coffee window 9.30-11am busy. Wi-Fi available; Jio strong, Airtel patchy. Cash and UPI; no card. Take-home coffee 250g ₹350.

belur.tagline: UNESCO Hoysala temple — Chennakesava's soapstone carvings are the most intricate in India

eateries.name: Hotel Mayura Velapuri (KSTDC)
eateries.why_it_matters: KSTDC heritage-property restaurant directly opposite the Chennakeshava temple gate — the standard lunch stop for the Hoysala-temple tour-bus convoy. Multi-cuisine veg + non-veg menu; mutton curry uses the regional Hassan-Coorg coriander-coconut base. The front desk doubles as the unofficial Hoysala-circuit information hub. Open 7am-10pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch (12.30-2pm) is the peak window for the tour-bus convoy. Order the Karnataka unlimited veg thali (₹300) for the most regional plate. Combine with morning temple visit; the property is 100m from the temple gate. UPI and cards both work; KSTDC pricing is fixed.

eateries.name: Hotel New Gayatri
eateries.why_it_matters: Pure-veg local anchor on the Belur main road — the workaday lunch stop for the temple priest community and pilgrim families doing the Chennakeshava darshan. Karnataka-style thali (ragi mudde + bisi bele bath + saagu + curd rice) is the regional anchor. Family-run since the 1990s. Open 6.30am-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch (12-2pm) fills with the post-darshan crowd. Order the ragi mudde thali — request it specifically since the menu defaults to chapati. Cash and UPI both work.

eateries.name: Adarsh Veg
eateries.area: Main Road, near Belur bus stand
eateries.why_it_matters: Local pure-veg tiffin counter near the Belur bus stand — the breakfast stop for the morning arrivals before the 8am Chennakeshava temple gate opening. Standard South Indian tiffin menu; khara bath + chow-chow bath is the regional breakfast convention. Plastic-table service, ceiling fans, no AC. Open 6.30am-10pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Pre-8am breakfast before the temple darshan rush. Khara bath sells out by 10am on weekends. Cash preferred; UPI works at the main counter.

eateries.name: Sri Devi Restaurant
eateries.area: Temple Road, opposite east tower (raja gopura)
eateries.why_it_matters: Pure-veg pilgrim-oriented restaurant directly opposite the Chennakeshava east tower — used by the post-darshan domestic-tourist crowd for a quick mid-day meal. Small hall, fan-cooled, family-table service. Veg thali ₹120 fixed; curd-rice + pickle is the standard summer order. Open 7am-9.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Post-temple lunch (1-2pm) is the peak window. Order the curd-rice + pickle combo on hot summer afternoons (40°C+ in Apr-May). Cash preferred; UPI inconsistent.

eateries.name: Hotel Annapoorna
eateries.why_it_matters: Local pure-veg sit-down on the Belur main road — the second-tier lunch alternative to New Gayatri, used by the bus-stand crowd and overnight pilgrim families. Bele saaru (Karnataka lentil soup) and ragi rotti are the regional anchors not always on New Gayatri's menu. Plastic tables, no AC. Open 6.30am-10pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch (12.30-2pm) is the peak. Ragi rotti (finger-millet flatbread) is served only on request. Cash and UPI both work.

bengaluru.tagline: India's Silicon Valley — craft beer capital, garden city, and the startup engine of a billion people

eateries.name: Glen's Bakehouse (Indiranagar)
eateries.why_it_matters: Started on 100 Feet Road in 2013 as a bakery-pizzeria hybrid; now sixteen-plus outlets across south India. The red velvet, tiramisu and wood-fired pizzas are the trio that built the brand.
eateries.insider_tip: Friday and Saturday night the queue runs an hour for desserts — go between 4pm and 6pm for fresh-out-of-the-oven slices and a free table. The bakehouse loaf is the locals' takeaway pick.
eateries.signature_address: 1027, 100 Feet Road, HAL 2nd Stage, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

eateries.name: Glen's Bakehouse (Lavelle Road)
eateries.why_it_matters: Founder Glen Williams (also of Sweet Chariot and Toit) opened the original on 100 Feet Road in 2013, then took over the old Java City spot on Lavelle Road in 2016. A live bakery and a hot kitchen under one roof — the closest Bengaluru gets to a European bakehouse-with-a-pub-feel.
eateries.insider_tip: The weekend roast is a sleeper hit — call ahead because portions sell out by 2pm. Sit upstairs at the Lavelle Road outlet for the quieter side of the room.

eateries.name: Hotel Janatha (Malleshwaram)
eateries.why_it_matters: A 1965 darshini on the same Sajjan Rao Circle stretch as the VV Puram food street, Janatha is one of two Basavanagudi names tied to the khali dosa — a soft, plain dosa eaten with coconut chutney. Workhorse menu, low prices, full at 8 am sharp.
eateries.insider_tip: Two sittings only — 6.30 am to noon and 3 pm to 7 pm. Order khali dosa with extra chutney; the masala version is solid but the plain one is what people return for.
eateries.signature_address: 26, Diagonal Road, Sajjan Rao Circle, VV Puram, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

eateries.name: Hotel Janatha (VV Puram)
eateries.why_it_matters: Old-school Malleshwaram tiffin room — thin, glistening Mysore masala dosa with a fierce red chutney lining and a filter coffee that locals rate above several flashier rivals. Tile-floor, vintage-board, walk-in-only kind of place.
eateries.insider_tip: Tuesday is Lord Hanuman day in this neighbourhood — Janatha gets slammed pre-temple. Aim for 8am or 11am off-peak. Order uddina vada with the dosa for the full Karnataka tiffin set.

eateries.name: Truffles (Indiranagar)
eateries.why_it_matters: Bengaluru's burger institution since 2004 — the chain that taught a generation of techies what a thick double-patty looks like. The Indiranagar outlet is the busiest in the group and the queue is part of the ritual.
eateries.insider_tip: Put your name on the host list and walk over to Toit or Glen's for an hour — they will SMS when your table is ready. Late lunch (3pm-4:30pm) is the only quiet window.
eateries.signature_address: Ground Floor, K.P. Square, 307, 100 Feet Road, Binnamangala, Stage 1, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

eateries.name: Mavalli Tiffin Rooms (MTR)
eateries.why_it_matters: Founded in 1924 by the Maiya brothers from Parampalli, MTR invented rava idli during WWII rice shortages and remains the city's most cited Udupi institution. The Lalbagh Road original is also one of only ~150 entries on the World's Legendary Restaurants list.
eateries.insider_tip: Take a token from the counter on entry, then wait upstairs for table service; the lunch thali (1 to 3 pm) is unlimited and the better-value meal vs. a dosa rush. Closed Mondays.

eateries.name: Vidyarthi Bhavan
eateries.why_it_matters: Started in 1943 as a tiny eatery for students of nearby colleges, Vidyarthi Bhavan's slow-cooked, ghee-soaked masala dosa is the benchmark Bengaluru measures all others against. The narrow Gandhi Bazaar shopfront and shared-table format have not changed in eight decades.
eateries.insider_tip: Arrive between 7 and 9 am on a weekday; the queue snakes around the lane after 10 am and wait times can hit 45 minutes. Closed Mondays. Cash and UPI only.
eateries.signature_address: 32, Gandhi Bazaar Main Road, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

eateries.name: CTR Shri Sagar (Central Tiffin Room)
eateries.why_it_matters: Established in 1920 by Y.V. Subramanyam, CTR is the city's reference point for benne (butter) masala dosa — crisp outer, soft inner, served with a thick coconut chutney. Now formally called Shri Sagar but locals still queue for what they grew up calling CTR.
eateries.insider_tip: The kitchen shuts between 12.30 pm and 4 pm — plan a breakfast or evening visit, not lunch. Pair the benne dosa with khara bath rather than a second dosa for the fuller flavour spread.
eateries.signature_address: 152, 7th Cross Road, Margosa Road, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560003

eateries.name: Brahmin's Coffee Bar
eateries.why_it_matters: Opened in 1965 by K.V. Nagesh Rao and K.N. Saraswati, Brahmin's serves only four things — idli, vada, khara bath, kesari bath — and is regularly named the city's best plate of soft idli with watery, mint-tinted coconut chutney. The same family runs it three generations on.
eateries.insider_tip: Stand-and-eat only, no chairs. Get there before 8.30 am to skip the office queue, and ask for the chutney refill — they pour generously if you don't waste the first cup. Closed Sundays.
eateries.signature_address: Ranga Rao Road, Near Shankar Mutt, Shankarapuram, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

eateries.name: Airlines Hotel
eateries.area: Madras Bank Road, off Lavelle Road
eateries.why_it_matters: The city's first drive-in restaurant, opened 1968 by Kalarickal Thomas and S.N. Rao. A century-old banyan shades the open-air tables and the kitchen pours close to 1,000 cups of filter coffee a day, mostly to office regulars who park up and stay an hour.
eateries.insider_tip: Eat in the garden, not the indoor section. Mornings 7-10am are the cleanest hour for coffee; the dosa batter peaks at breakfast.
eateries.signature_address: 4 Madras Bank Road, off Lavelle Road, Bengaluru 560001

eateries.name: Veena Stores
eateries.why_it_matters: A standing-only counter on 15th Cross since 1977, Veena Stores is the place locals send first-timers when they want to argue that Malleshwaram has the city's softest idli. The chutney spread (coconut, mint, peanut) is unusually generous for a street counter.
eateries.insider_tip: Open all seven days, 7 am to noon and 4 pm onwards. Ask for an extra chutney pour at the counter — they'll oblige if you don't push. UPI works; carry small notes for the tip.
eateries.signature_address: 187, 15th Cross, Margosa Road, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560003

eateries.name: New Modern Hotel
eateries.why_it_matters: Opened 1959 near Minerva Circle, NMH was a gathering room for Kannada writers (DVG, H.V. Seetharamaiah) and theatre figures (Girish Kasaravalli) — its masala dosa and rich badam halwa are both Basavanagudi reference dishes. Lodging-and-boarding format from a different era.
eateries.insider_tip: Be in by 9 am to avoid the office rush. Order the masala dosa with a side of badam halwa — sweet first or last is a long-running local debate worth settling for yourself.
eateries.signature_address: 143, Dr. A.N. Krishna Rao Road, Near Minerva Circle, VV Puram, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

eateries.name: Hotel Dwaraka
eateries.why_it_matters: Started 1972 on Bull Temple Road and now in NR Colony, Hotel Dwaraka is widely credited as the originator of Bengaluru's kali dosa — a soft, oil-less dosa cooked on a closed pan that arrived to the city before any other restaurant put it on a menu. Cash-only, self-service.
eateries.insider_tip: Cash only, no card or wallet. Avarekalu khara bath is seasonal (Dec to Feb when local field beans are in) — ask before ordering, it's the better khara bath outside the season.
eateries.signature_address: 7th Cross, NR Colony, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

eateries.name: Vasudev Adiga's
eateries.why_it_matters: K.N. Vasudev Adiga, son of Brahmin's Coffee Bar founder K.V. Nageshwar Adiga, opened the first Adiga's on DVG Road in 1993 as a clean, low-priced darshini. The chain is now the city's reference quality bar for what a darshini should taste like — same recipes across 12+ Bengaluru outlets.
eateries.insider_tip: The Jayanagar 4th Block branch runs a faster turnaround than the AC restaurants — pay first at the counter, then collect from the kitchen window. Best for a 15-minute weekday breakfast stop.

eateries.name: The Fatty Bao
eateries.why_it_matters: Olive Bar and Kitchen's pan-Asian gastrobar — the Indiranagar rooftop where Bengaluru learnt to take steamed bao seriously. Chocolate dim sum dessert is now copied across India.
eateries.insider_tip: Sit on the open terrace for the after-work crowd; the indoor bar gets loud after 9pm. The bao platter plus a single khow suey feeds two comfortably without ordering mains.
eateries.signature_address: 610, 3rd Floor, 12th Main Road, Off 80 Feet Road, HAL 2nd Stage, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560008

eateries.name: The Permit Room
eateries.why_it_matters: Indian gastropub that pulls food from five southern states — Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra, Telangana and Tamil Nadu — and pairs them with filter-coffee cocktails and tap beer. The format that nudged Bengaluru's bar food past kebabs.
eateries.insider_tip: Order the kerala parotta with beef ularthiyathu plus one filter-coffee old fashioned — that's the signature combo. Tuesday and Wednesday are calmest; weekends need a 7pm or earlier slot.
eateries.signature_address: 55, Lower Palace Orchards, 100 Feet Road, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

eateries.name: Third Wave Coffee Roasters
eateries.why_it_matters: Bengaluru's homegrown answer to global third-wave coffee — co-founders Anirudh Sharma, Ayush Bathwal and Sushant Goel set up the first specialty cafe-roastery of its kind in the country in Koramangala, then scaled to 100+ outlets. The Indiranagar room is where the brand still feels closest to its roastery roots.
eateries.insider_tip: Order the single-estate pour over of the week — the barista will quote the farm and altitude unprompted. Skip the flavoured lattes; the milk-and-bean ratios are tuned for the flat white and cortado.
eateries.signature_address: Ground Floor, 80 30th Feet Main Road, CMH Road, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

eateries.name: The Hole in the Wall Cafe
eateries.why_it_matters: Started in 2009 by Bangalore couple Lynn Dcosta and Nathan Harris in a no-frills garage — became the city's de facto Sunday brunch institution. Continental breakfast done honestly, affordably, and the same way for 17 years. Mondays closed, weekend queues cheerful.
eateries.insider_tip: No reservations — show up before 9am on Saturday or after 11.30am Sunday to skip the worst of the wait. Closed Mondays. The all-day breakfast is the move; the dinner menu is forgettable.

eateries.name: Dyu Art Cafe
eateries.signature_dish: filter coffee with the day's sandwich
eateries.why_it_matters: A restored Kerala-style heritage home with open courtyard, oxide flooring and gabled roof — the rotating gallery wall has hung work by city-based and visiting artists for over a decade. Set the tone for Koramangala's cafe culture before the area went mainstream.
eateries.insider_tip: Sit in the courtyard, not the upstairs gallery — the light is better and you can hear the bird call from the mango tree. Closed early evenings some weekdays; check before driving across town.
eateries.signature_address: 23/22, 1st Cross Road, KHB MIG Colony, Koramangala 8th Block, Bengaluru 560095

eateries.name: Mahesh Lunch Home
must_try: neer dosa with chicken ghee roast
eateries.why_it_matters: Bengaluru outpost of S.C. Karkera's Mangalorean institution founded in Mumbai in 1977. The chef-brings-the-tray-of-fish ritual and butter garlic mussels remain unchanged across forty-plus years.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunchtime thali with surmai, bangda and a neer dosa is the cheapest way in; a la carte at dinner runs nearly double. Pick your fish from the chef's tray before ordering — that's how regulars get the freshest catch.
eateries.signature_address: 2011, 1st Floor, 100 Feet Road, HAL 2nd Stage, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

eateries.name: Halli Mane
eateries.why_it_matters: Halli Mane (Kannada for 'village home') is the city's most cited address for rural Karnataka vegetarian cooking — ragi mudde, akki rotti, jolada rotti, bisi bele bath, obbattu — served on banana leaves in a low-seating, village-themed room. Operating on Sampige Road for 20+ years.
eateries.insider_tip: The unlimited weekend breakfast buffet is the best value way to taste eight to ten Karnataka village dishes in one sitting. Ask the server which obbattu (holige) filling is freshest that day — coconut, dal or jaggery.
eateries.signature_address: 14, 3rd Cross, Sampige Road, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560003

eateries.name: Toit Brewpub
eateries.why_it_matters: Founded in 2010 by Sibi Venkataraju, Arun George and Mukesh Tolani, Toit is the brewpub that put Bengaluru on India's craft beer map. The three-floor 100 Feet Road flagship still pulls weekend queues for the Toit Weiss and Tintin Toit on tap.
eateries.insider_tip: Walk in before 6:30pm on a weekday for the rooftop and you'll skip the 90-minute wait that builds after 7pm. The Toit Weiss is the safer first pour than the rotating seasonals.
eateries.signature_address: 298, 100 Feet Road, Binnamangala, Stage 1, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

eateries.name: Karavalli
eateries.why_it_matters: Open since 1990 inside what is now Vivanta Bengaluru Residency Road, Karavalli is India's longest-running fine-dining south-west-coast restaurant. The tamarind-tree garden room and chef Naren Thimmaiah's recipes are the textbook reference for Mangalorean, Coorgi and Kerala-coast cooking.
eateries.insider_tip: Reserve the open verandah seating, not the indoor wood-panel room — the garden is the experience. Ask the captain for the off-menu daily catch from the crab and karimeen tray.
eateries.signature_address: Vivanta Bengaluru Residency Road, 41/3 Mahatma Gandhi Road, Bengaluru 560025

eateries.name: Smoke House Deli
eateries.why_it_matters: Riyaaz Amlani's Impresario all-day deli, born 2009 — the format that gave Indian metros their first credible take on smoked meats, hand-drawn-mural cafes and brunch-as-a-routine. Indiranagar branch is the city's go-to brunch booking.
eateries.insider_tip: Sunday brunch packs the room from noon — book the corner banquette near the bar for the calmest seating. The english breakfast plus a smoked chicken sandwich split between two is the value play.
eateries.signature_address: Ward 72, Plot 1209, 100 Feet Road, HAL 2nd Stage, Doopanahalli, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

eateries.name: Meghana Foods
eateries.why_it_matters: The Andhra biryani most copied in Bengaluru — operating since 2006, the Koramangala 5th Block flagship is the city's go-to for spice-heavy chicken and mutton biryani. Queues form even on weekday evenings.
eateries.insider_tip: Token system: collect a token at the entrance, then loop back when called rather than standing in line. Order extra raita and salan — both are part of the biryani's character. Skip dinner peak (8-10pm) for 30+ minute waits.
eateries.signature_address: 124, 1st A Cross Road, 5th Block, Koramangala, Bengaluru 560095

eateries.name: Nagarjuna
must_try: andhra veg meal on banana leaf
eateries.why_it_matters: Founded 1984 by N. Krishna Reddy as the original outlet, this Residency Road branch is the template every Andhra meals chain in the city imitates. Unlimited rice, ghee and ten-plus accompaniments served on a banana leaf.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch (12-3pm) is when the meals are freshest — by dinner the spread thins. Outlets in Koramangala and Indiranagar follow the same recipe, but the Residency Road original still pulls regulars after four decades.
eateries.signature_address: 44/1, Residency Road, near Mayo Hall, Shanthala Nagar, Bengaluru 560025

eateries.name: Le Cirque Signature
eateries.why_it_matters: Indian outpost of the Manhattan institution founded by Sirio Maccioni in 1974, opened at The Leela Palace in 2014. The only Franco-Italian fine-dining room of this pedigree in south India — wine list runs to 250+ labels and the imported French cheese trolley is the city's largest.
eateries.insider_tip: Dinner-only — open 6:30pm to 11:30pm. Skip the à la carte and book the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing; it works out cheaper than ordering three courses solo.
eateries.signature_address: The Leela Palace Bengaluru, 23 HAL Old Airport Road, Kodihalli, Bengaluru 560008

eateries.name: The Royal Afghan
eateries.why_it_matters: Poolside open-air kebab institution at ITC Windsor since the hotel opened in 1982 — the same menu for over four decades. The dal bukhara has simmered for 24 hours every day for 40+ years, and the kakori is still minced and skewered to the original ITC recipe that put north-west frontier cuisine on India's hotel-restaurant map.
eateries.insider_tip: Book a poolside table after sunset — the open-flame tandoor sits in plain sight and the smoke hits differently outdoors. Lunch is rarely full; dinner needs a week's notice on weekends.
eateries.signature_address: ITC Windsor, 25 Windsor Square, Golf Course Road, Bengaluru 560052

eateries.name: Toscano
must_try: goat cheese rucola and pear salad with parmaham
eateries.why_it_matters: Founded by Chefs Jean Michel Jasserand and Goutham Balasubramanian, the UB City flagship is Bengaluru's longest-running Italian fine-dining room. Times Food Award 'Best Italian Restaurant in Bangalore' multiple years; the pasta is rolled in-house daily and the wine list is the deepest Italian-only selection in the city.
eateries.insider_tip: Sit on the outdoor terrace facing Vittal Mallya Road — the only UB City restaurant with proper alfresco seating. The four-course set lunch on weekdays is the value play.
eateries.signature_address: Level 3, UB City Mall, 24 Vittal Mallya Road, Bengaluru 560001

eateries.name: Koshy's
eateries.why_it_matters: P.O. Koshy opened the bakery in 1940 and the Parade Cafe followed on St Mark's Road in 1952; Nehru, Khrushchev, Marshal Tito and Queen Elizabeth II were all catered to here. Three generations on, the wood-panelled hall still pulls journalists, lawyers and old Bangaloreans for breakfast and beer.
eateries.insider_tip: Open 9am-11.30pm. The bar (Jewel Box) on the side is the writers' corner; the main hall is breakfast country. Cash and UPI both work.
eateries.signature_address: 39 St Mark's Road, Shanthala Nagar, Bengaluru 560001

eateries.name: Empire Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Abdul Rahim Haji took over a Central Street eatery in 1966 and renamed it after MG Road's old Empire Theatre; the late-1980s 'coin parotta' — a leftover-dough accident — became the cult dish. From this Mosque Road kitchen the family has grown a 45-outlet, ₹560 crore Bengaluru chain.
eateries.insider_tip: Open till 4am — the post-pub biryani run is the local move. The Mosque Road outlet is the original; queues from 9pm.

eateries.name: Maverick & Farmer Coffee
eateries.why_it_matters: Founded in 2018 by Sreeram G, Tej Thammaiah and Ashish D'abreo — one of India's few bean-to-cup roasters that grow on their own Coorg estate. The lab-style menu (cold-smoked coffee, clarified cappuccino, fermented experiments) put Bengaluru's specialty scene on the global map.
eateries.insider_tip: Ask for the cupping flight if it's running — the barista will walk you through three estates side by side. The clarified cappuccino is the conversation starter; the cherry soda is the surprise.
eateries.signature_address: 118, 5th B Cross Road, Koramangala 4th Block, Bengaluru 560034

eateries.name: Truffles (Koramangala)
eateries.why_it_matters: The benchmark Bengaluru burger — generous patties, fries and milkshakes that built the city's casual-burger template before the global chains arrived. Now eight dine-in outlets, with the Koramangala 5th Block branch the busiest after St. Marks Road.
eateries.insider_tip: Weekend evening waits hit 60-90 minutes; go weekday lunch 12:30-1:30 or late afternoon 4-6 to walk in. The Koramangala outlet is closer to the original feel than the newer Indiranagar 100 Feet Road branch.
eateries.signature_address: 28, 4th B Cross Road, 5th Block, Koramangala, Bengaluru 560095

eateries.name: Windmills Craftworks
eateries.why_it_matters: Opened 2012 in Whitefield as India's first integrated jazz theatre and microbrewery, with a curated design library on the same floor. Wednesday-Saturday evenings host live jazz, blues and fusion acts that tech-park regulars build dinners around.
eateries.insider_tip: Reserve the jazz theatre side (separate from the bar) for the live-music nights — bar-side seats hear the music but miss the room. Cover charges apply on headliner nights; check the calendar before booking.
eateries.signature_address: 6th Floor, 331, Road 5B, EPIP Zone, Whitefield, Bengaluru 560066

eateries.name: Chianti Ristorante & Wine Bar
eateries.why_it_matters: Koramangala's long-running Italian — first opened here over a decade ago, now seven outlets across the city. The original 5th Block flagship still sets the bar for honest pasta and wood-fired pizza without fine-dining theatre.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch sets are the value play: two courses for under ₹1000 weekdays. Reserve a window booth on the upper level; ground-floor tables are louder once the bar fills up after 8pm.

eateries.name: Anand Sweets & Savouries
eateries.why_it_matters: Founded 1988 by Anand Dadu — Bengaluru's market-leading premium mithai chain. 15 city stores, airport retail at 15 Indian airports, and a flagship in Jayanagar that's the default sweet-box for weddings and Diwali across Karnataka.
eateries.insider_tip: Order at the takeaway counter for sweet-boxes; the small dine-in serves chaat and chole bhature for the wait. Festival season (Diwali, Sankranti) — order kesar badam barfi 2 days ahead.
eateries.signature_address: Shop 4 & 5, D No 14/39, 27th Cross, 4th Block, Jayanagar, Bengaluru 560041

eateries.name: Taaza Thindi
eateries.why_it_matters: Self-service breakfast counter run by the Mayura Group (founded 1976) — fluffy rava idli, ghee-soaked khara bath and a 4.9 Zomato rating that locals defend like a local stock. One of the cleanest, fastest South-Indian tiffin counters in the city.
eateries.insider_tip: Open 7am-12pm and 4pm-9:30pm; rava idli batch is hottest before 9am. Pay at the cashier first, then take the chit to the counter. UPI works.
eateries.signature_address: 1004, Ground Floor, Next to HDFC Bank, 26th Main Road, Jayanagar 4th T Block, Bengaluru 560041

eateries.name: Hari Super Sandwich
eateries.why_it_matters: Bengaluru's most famous sandwich counter — a tiny pure-veg shop on VV Puram Food Street that fills you up under ₹100 with sandwiches and chaat the city has crowned a street-food institution.
eateries.insider_tip: Crowds peak 7pm-10pm — go right at 5pm opening for the freshest bread. The chocolate sandwich sounds like a stunt; it is a stunt that works. Standing-only, eat on the street.
eateries.signature_address: 2, National High School Road, VV Puram, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru 560004

eateries.name: Burma Burma
eateries.why_it_matters: All-vegetarian Burmese — khow suey, tea-leaf salad and samuza hincho (samosa-in-broth) that introduced Bengaluru to a cuisine it had no template for. Three city outlets (Indiranagar, Brigade Road, Yelahanka) and a no-alcohol policy that keeps it food-first.
eateries.insider_tip: No reservations — first-come-first-served. Arrive 6:30pm sharp for dinner or face a 45-minute wait. The dedicated tea menu is genuinely good; try a Burmese milk tea flight alongside the khow suey rather than defaulting to soft drinks.
eateries.signature_address: 607, 12th Main Road, 7th Cross, HAL 2nd Stage, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

eateries.name: The Rameshwaram Cafe
eateries.why_it_matters: The viral 2023-2024 South Indian quick-service phenomenon — ghee podi idli and benne masala dosa served counter-style at sub-₹100 price points. The Brookefield outlet reopened on 8 March 2024 after the on-premise blast and remains operational with the same crowds it had before.
eateries.insider_tip: Breakfast (7-10am) is when the idlis and dosas are freshest and the wait is shortest. By 11am queues stretch outside. Order at the counter, collect from the next station — the system rewards arriving solo or in pairs over big groups.
eateries.signature_address: Plot No. 1, Green Avenue, ITPL Main Road, Brookefield, Bengaluru 560037

eateries.name: Jamavar
eateries.why_it_matters: The Leela Palace's flagship Indian room, named after the Kashmiri brocade and built around a regional survey of dum-cooked north and south Indian classics. Awarded by La Liste in both 2025 (82.5) and 2026 (80) — one of the few Karnataka restaurants on that global list. Chef Sahadevan handles south Indian, Chef Jasbir runs the north Indian section.
eateries.insider_tip: Request a garden-terrace table for dinner and pre-order the raan — it needs 24 hours to braise. The vegetarian dum biryani is the quiet hero non-veg diners regret missing.
eateries.signature_address: The Leela Palace Bengaluru, 23 HAL Old Airport Road, Kodihalli, Bengaluru 560008

eateries.name: Yauatcha
eateries.why_it_matters: Hakkasan Group's Bengaluru dim sum house — same kitchen lineage as the Michelin-starred London original. The all-day dim sum tea-house format runs 40+ steamed, baked and fried varieties plus a French-trained patisserie counter; opened at 1 MG in 2014 and still the city's gold standard for Cantonese fine dining.
eateries.insider_tip: Dim sum lunch is half the dinner price for the same kitchen and skill. The vegetarian dim sum platter is one of India's best — the truffle edamame dumpling alone justifies the trip.
eateries.signature_address: Level 5, 1 MG Lido Mall, MG Road, Bengaluru 560001

eateries.name: Indian Coffee House
eateries.why_it_matters: The Bengaluru cooperative was formed in 1957, the original MG Road branch ran from 1959 until April 2009, and the Workers' Cooperative reopened it on Church Street the same year — same turbaned waiters, same red-and-white interior, same prices that haven't moved with the city.
eateries.insider_tip: Behind Shringar Shopping Complex on Church Street. The cutlets are made fresh after 4pm; mornings are coffee-and-paper crowd.
eateries.signature_address: G-37 & 38, Indian Coffee House, Ground Floor, behind Shringar Shopping Complex, Church Street, Bengaluru 560001

eateries.name: Albert Bakery
eateries.why_it_matters: Mohammed Suleman opened it in 1902 and named it after Prince Albert to court Frazer Town's Anglo clientele; the great-grandson Sabir runs it today. During Ramzan the queue for bheja (goat brain) puffs and mutton samosas wraps around Mosque Road every evening.
eateries.insider_tip: Opens 3pm, closes by 7-8pm — go before 5pm or join the queue. Cash easier than card. During Ramzan the food street outside is the bigger experience.

eateries.name: The Only Place
eateries.why_it_matters: Haroon Sait opened it in 1965 to feed the Peace Corps Americans and Iranian guests staying at his family's hotel — a Japanese diner suggested the name because it was the only place serving steaks and apple pie in the city. The 40-year-old apple pie recipe and the steaks are both unchanged.
eateries.insider_tip: Now on Museum Road in a 150-seater with park-bench seating; the older Brigade Road outpost has shut. The al fresco section is the one to ask for.

eateries.name: Imperial Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Running since 1954, Imperial is one of the city's two surviving vintage Mughlai chains — Cunningham Road is the original. The biryani-and-fried-chicken-kebab combo is a Bangalore late-night ritual and the kitchen stays open until 1am.
eateries.insider_tip: Open till 1am — many regulars come post-cinema. Original outlet is on Cunningham; the Residency Road and Indiranagar branches are newer.

eateries.name: VB Bakery
eateries.why_it_matters: Visvesvarapuram Brahmin Bakery — landmark Iyengar bakery at the entrance of VV Puram Food Street, 65+ years old. Many credit it with seeding the Iyengar-bakery template now copied across south Bengaluru.
eateries.insider_tip: Get here before 7pm — the khara bun ("KBC") with spicy peanut filling sells out by mid-evening. Pair with a Mangalore bun next door. Cash and UPI both work.
eateries.signature_address: 1, Sajjan Rao Circle, VV Puram, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru 560004

eateries.name: Bhagatram Sweets
eateries.why_it_matters: Started 1948 by Bhagatram, a Sindhi migrant who landed in Bengaluru via Delhi, Mumbai and Chennai. The Commercial Street counter feeds ~4,000 people a day and is the city's reference for North Indian-style mithai and chole bhature.
eateries.insider_tip: Saturday afternoons and festival eves are pure scrum — go weekday 11am or 4pm. Stand at the chaat counter for the dahi vada, then queue separately at the sweets counter. UPI works; cash for fastest service.

eateries.name: Lavonne Cafe
eateries.why_it_matters: Started in 2012 by pastry chefs Vinesh Johny, Avin Thaliath and Lijo Chandy as the country's first international baking and pastry arts academy with a cafe attached — every dessert leaving the counter is school-grade. This is the dessert benchmark every other Bengaluru patisserie is measured against.
eateries.insider_tip: The custom cake counter takes 48-hour notice for the entremets — worth it for a birthday. Walk-in for the tartes and croissants midweek; weekend mall traffic kills the experience.
eateries.signature_address: Lower Ground Floor, Forum Shantiniketan Mall, ITPL Main Road, Whitefield, Bengaluru 560048

stays.name: Raintree Hotel St Marks
stays.why_special: Heritage-style boutique hotel in the heart of the city. Rooftop bar, walkable to all MG Road attractions. Good base for Bengaluru.

stays.name: Zostel Bengaluru
stays.why_special: Best backpacker hostel. Common area buzzing with travelers. Pub crawl nights, free walking tours. Koramangala location for craft beer scene.

picks.name: ITC Windsor
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for its position in Bangalore's Residency Road corridor—walking distance to MG Road shops, restaurants, and the central business district.

eateries.name: Hotel Suvarna Residency Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: AC mid-range restaurant inside Hotel Suvarna Residency — one of Bidar's two-three full-service multi-cuisine sit-downs. Mughlai-leaning menu reflects the Bahmani-era Persian-Deccan culinary thread that distinguishes Bidar from south Karnataka. Mutton biryani here uses sesame oil and short-grain rice (north Karnataka style, not the Hyderabadi long-grain). Open 7am-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch 1-2.30pm fills with government visitors and archaeology survey teams. Order the Mughlai non-veg thali (mutton kabab + chicken curry + rice + paratha + dal) for a single comprehensive Deccan plate. UPI and cards both work.

eateries.name: Hotel Mayura Barid Shahi (KSTDC)
eateries.area: Udgir Road, near Bidar Fort entrance
eateries.why_it_matters: KSTDC heritage-property restaurant just outside the Bidar Fort gate — used by heritage tourists doing the Bidar-Gulbarga-Bijapur Deccan Sultanate circuit. Multi-cuisine menu with a regional Deccan-Mughlai section. The KSTDC desk also coordinates ASI guides and Karez tour bookings, making this the de-facto information hub. Open 7am-10pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Combine lunch here with the morning fort circuit — the property sits 200m from the Sharza Darwaza fort entrance. Pre-book the KSTDC Karez tour at the front desk a day ahead. UPI and cards both work; the KSTDC pricing is fixed and printed.

eateries.name: Sahara Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Local Mughlai non-veg anchor near Mailoor Cross — the regional biryani standard for Bidar. Bidar-style biryani uses short-grain rice (not Hyderabadi long-grain), sesame oil, and a heavier black-pepper masala from the Bahmani-era spice route. Open 11am-11pm; peak lunch 1-2.30pm and dinner 7.30-10pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Order the mutton biryani (chicken is good, mutton is the signature). Friday 12.30-2.30pm fills with the post-namaz crowd. Cash and UPI; small AC section at the back, fan section at the front. Closes briefly during Ramzan iftar hours — call ahead.

eateries.name: Karan Veg Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Pure-veg counter on Udgir Road serving the local Jain/Marwadi business community and pilgrims to Nanak Jhira Sahib. North Karnataka jolada roti thali is the regional anchor — served with brinjal ennegayi (stuffed eggplant), peanut chutney, dal, and curd. Also runs a strong pav-bhaji and South Indian tiffin counter. Open 7am-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Jolada roti thali peaks 12.30-2pm — order by 1pm before the office lunch crowd. Pav bhaji is the evening (6-8pm) regional speciality, served with extra butter. Cash and UPI both.

eateries.name: Adarsh Bhavan
eateries.area: Old Bidar bazaar, near Gandhi Gunj

Operates on a tiffin + filter coffee model; the khara bath here is the regional speciality (savoury semolina with green chillies + curry leaves + curd-style buttermilk on the side). Open 6.30am-11.30am + 4-8.30pm; closed afternoons.
eateries.insider_tip: Pre-9am for the freshest tiffin. Khara bath sells out by 10am on weekends. Old bazaar location means parking is tight — auto-rickshaw is the easier access. Cash preferred; UPI works at the main counter.

North Karnataka jolada roti thali (sorghum flatbread + brinjal ennegayi + jaggery + dal + buttermilk) is the regional anchor. Bele holige (jaggery-stuffed flatbread) is the festival speciality. eateries.insider_tip: Lunch 12.30-2pm fills with government and business visitors. Order the unlimited thali (₹250) on weekdays; weekend buffet (₹350) covers more regional items. UPI and cards both work. Skip Sundays — religious processions sometimes close the road.

Mughlai-leaning menu reflects the Adil Shahi-era Persian-Deccan culinary thread. Mutton biryani uses short-grain rice (north Karnataka style, not Hyderabadi long-grain). Open 7am-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Dinner 8-10pm is the peak window. Order the Bijapuri mutton biryani over chicken — the regional black-pepper masala is heavier than Hyderabadi style. Pre-book on weekends; cards and UPI both.

eateries.name: Sabir Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Local Mughlai non-veg biryani anchor at Gandhi Chowk — the regional standard for Bijapuri-style biryani. Family-run since the 1980s; uses short-grain rice + sesame oil + a heavy black-pepper masala distinct from both Hyderabadi and Lucknowi styles. Open 11am-11pm; peak lunch 1-2.30pm and dinner 7.30-10pm. Fan section at the front; AC section at the rear.
eateries.insider_tip: Order mutton biryani over chicken — the regional anchor. Friday 12.30-2.30pm fills with post-namaz crowd. Sheermal (saffron-tinged sweet flatbread) is the dessert-style accompaniment if available. Cash and UPI both. Closes briefly during Ramzan iftar — call ahead.

eateries.name: Hotel Kanishka
eateries.why_it_matters: AC multi-cuisine restaurant inside Hotel Kanishka — second-tier behind Madhuvan and Pearl but reliably open and used as a backup when the others are full. Standard north Karnataka regional + Mughlai non-veg + South Indian tiffin menu. Open 7am-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: If Madhuvan and Pearl are both full (Saturdays especially), Kanishka is the third option. Veg buffet on weekend lunches (₹300 fixed). UPI and cards both work.

eateries.name: Karnataka Lunch Home

North Karnataka jolada roti thali is the regional anchor; this is the lower-budget alternative to Madhuvan's AC dining. Plastic tables, ceiling fans, family-table style service. Open 7am-10pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch 12.30-2pm peaks with the office and trader crowd. Order the unlimited jolada roti thali (₹120) — bele holige (jaggery flatbread) is served on festival days. Cash preferred; small UPI display.

eateries.name: Hotel Sri Annapurna

stays.why_special: Coffee estate homestay with panoramic valley views. Kodava family-run. Home-cooked pandi curry that guests travel back for. Misty mornings on the verandah.

stays.name: Honey Valley Estate
stays.why_special: Budget backpacker favorite. Basic rooms in a coffee estate. Communal meals, bonfire, trekking starting point. The kind of place where you extend your stay.

picks.name: The Tamara Coorg

dharmasthala.tagline: The temple that feeds 30,000 people free every day — Dharmasthala's annadana tradition

eateries.name: Annadana (Annapurna Bhojanashala) at Manjunatha Temple
eateries.why_it_matters: Centuries-old free mass-feeding tradition at the Manjunatha Temple — 30,000-50,000 pilgrims served daily, scaling to 1-2 lakh on weekends and ~5 lakh on major festival days (Lakshadeepotsava in November). The kitchen runs three shifts (breakfast 7-10am, lunch 11.30am-3pm, dinner 7-9pm), staffed by 600+ volunteers + cooks; rice and vegetables are donated by devotees through the Trust. The annadana is what makes Dharmasthala the highest-footfall pilgrimage centre in Karnataka after Tirupati for free-meal pilgrims.
eateries.insider_tip: Free meal hall opens 30 min before each session — arrive 15 min early for shorter queue. Banana-leaf service, sit cross-legged on the floor in long rows; mobile phones not permitted inside hall. The payasam at lunch is the consistent sweet across all days.

eateries.name: Hotel Sharadhi
eateries.why_it_matters: Main bazaar pilgrim restaurant — the most consistent paid alternative to the temple annadana, for pilgrims wanting a quicker private meal or breakfast outside the temple-meal timings. The veg meals (₹120) is the lunch order; the masala dosa (₹60) is the busy-breakfast default. Open 6am-10pm; pure-veg, no onion/garlic.
eateries.insider_tip: Breakfast 6.30-9am and post-darshan lunch 1.30-3pm are the busiest windows. Cash + UPI; no card terminal. The Mangalore buns + sambar combo (₹70) is a Tulu Nadu pilgrim breakfast staple.
eateries.signature_address: Main bazaar, opposite Manjunatha temple gate, Dharmasthala 574216

eateries.name: Hotel Sagar
eateries.why_it_matters: Bus stand-side pilgrim canteen — useful for bus arrivals and departures off-hours when the temple annadana is between sessions. Idli + vada + filter coffee combo (₹70) is the breakfast and tiffin staple. Pure-veg, no onion/garlic; open 5.30am-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Pre-bus 5.30-6am for breakfast — fresh idli batter at 6am sharp. The chai-vada window at 4-6pm is the busiest after the post-darshan crowd. Cash + UPI.

eateries.name: Hotel Sukrut

The sweet originates from Gokak (60km north) but the Gulbarga preparation is the more refined version using local Bidar jaggery. Also a strong chaat and tiffin counter for the evening crowd. eateries.insider_tip: Karadant is the must-buy — comes in 250g and 500g vacuum-packed slabs (₹400-700) that travel well. Buy fresh batch (made Mon and Thu); ask the counter about the prep day. Pav bhaji and falooda are the regional evening (6-8pm) snacks. Cash and UPI both.

Operates on a thali + tiffin model: Karnataka-style veg thali ₹120, individual tiffin items ₹40-80. Tin-roof + plastic-table service; no AC, ceiling fans only. Open 7am-7pm; closed by 8pm since the temple gate closes 6.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch (12.30-2pm) fills with the post-darshan crowd. Thali is the simplest order; curd-rice + pickle for hot summer afternoons. Cash preferred; UPI inconsistent. Carry water — no proper supply after this on the road back to Belur or Hassan.

eateries.name: Sri Krishna Refreshments
eateries.area: Main Road, Halebidu village (300m from temple gate)
eateries.why_it_matters: Local pure-veg breakfast counter on the Halebidu village main road — the morning stop before the 8am temple gate opening. Standard South Indian tiffin menu; khara bath + chow-chow bath is the regional breakfast convention. Small hall (5-6 plastic tables), fan-cooled, no AC. Open 6.30am-3pm; no dinner service.
eateries.insider_tip: Pre-8am breakfast before the temple darshan rush. By 10am the tour buses arrive and parking fills the main road. Cash preferred; UPI inconsistent.

eateries.name: Hassan Adyar Anand Bhavan (16km base)
eateries.why_it_matters: Halebidu village has no dinner option — most overnight visitors base in Hassan (16km / 30 min drive) and use the verified Adyar Anand Bhavan Hassan branch. The chain (founded 1964 Madras, expanded across Karnataka) is the regional Chennai-Karnataka dosa-and-tiffin standard. AC hall, family-table service. Open 7am-11pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Plan Halebidu + Belur as morning trips (8am-2pm) and return to Hassan for lunch or dinner. Mini tiffin (4-5 small portions) is the chain's breakfast convention. UPI and cards both. The Hassan branch is on the main BM Road, easy to find.

eateries.name: Hoysala Village Resort Restaurant (Hassan base)
eateries.why_it_matters: AC mid-range restaurant inside Hoysala Village Resort on the Belur-Hassan road — the heritage-style resort used by overnight Hoysala-circuit visitors. Multi-cuisine veg + non-veg menu including a Karnataka regional section. The de-facto overnight-stay anchor for Halebidu day-trippers since Halebidu village has no dinner option. Open 7am-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Pre-book for dinner if not a resort guest. Mutton biryani is the regional non-veg call; Karnataka veg thali for the regional veg plate. The resort grounds are pleasant for a 7pm pre-dinner walk; the Hoysala-style stone-carved gateposts are a nice touch. UPI and cards both work.

eateries.name: Itihakala Restaurant
must_try: unlimited Karnataka thali on banana leaf
eateries.why_it_matters: Halebidu village has historically had thin sit-down options for the UNESCO-listed Hoysaleswara Temple traffic. Itihakala opened as a pure-veg eco-build (wood, stone, cane) 1km from the temple, run by owner Sunil. Unlimited Karnataka thali on banana leaf is the regional anchor — holige (sweet stuffed flatbread), dry vegetable palyas, akki rotti. Halebidu+Belur+Somnathpur joint UNESCO inscription was September 2023, so this is the first decade of formalised tourism food infrastructure here.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch fills 12:30-14:30 with the tour-bus circuit (Belur→Halebidu→Shravanabelagola). Pre-noon (11:30) or post-15:00 is calmer. Cash works best; UPI sometimes patchy on the village line. Two seatings: 11:00-15:30 and 19:00-21:30.
eateries.signature_address: 1km from Hoysaleswara Temple, Hagare-Itihakala Road, Halebeedu, Karnataka 573121

picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for honest home-cooked meals, owner-led temple walks, and rates that free up budget for guides and travel—best experience-per-rupee in the Hassan district.

picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for its working coffee and spice farm 40 km west, where travellers harvest with farmers before dawn, then study stone carving in Halebidu by afternoon—a rare dual-rhythm stay.

hampi.tagline: UNESCO ruins of a forgotten empire — boulders, temples, and the ghost of Vijayanagara

eateries.name: Mango Tree Restaurant
eateries.area: Virupapur Gaddi (Hippie Island), Tungabhadra north bank
eateries.signature_dish: Thali on the river-side mango tree platform
eateries.why_it_matters: Hampi's longest-running riverside cafe, named for the massive mango tree under which it operates on the Hippie Island (Virupapur Gaddi) side of the Tungabhadra. Originally opened in the early 2000s; relocated from the south bank to the north after Karnataka High Court demolitions inside the heritage zone (2011). Floor cushions on stepped river terraces, Hindi-Hebrew menu reflecting the Israeli backpacker base, slow service is the norm.
eateries.insider_tip: Sunset from 5.30-6.30pm is the peak booking window — arrive 4.30pm to claim a riverfront cushion. Order the thali before 1pm; kitchen runs slow on weekends. Coracle crossing from Hampi Bazaar side last ferry 5.30pm — plan dinner before that or stay overnight on Hippie Island.

eateries.name: Laughing Buddha
eateries.why_it_matters: Hippie Island institution since the mid-2000s — wooden deck cantilevered over the Tungabhadra with the Virupaksha temple gopura framed in the distance. Mixed Israeli + Italian + Indian menu reflects the long-stay backpacker base (most guests stay 2-4 weeks). Cushion seating, slow Wi-Fi, no AC, mosquito coils after sunset. Open 7am-10.30pm; closes during monsoon (mid-Jun to mid-Sep).
eateries.insider_tip: Best view in Hampi at sunset — claim a front-row cushion 30 min before sunset (6pm Oct-Mar). Wood-fired pizza takes 25-30 min; order before the sunset rush. Coracle last ferry to Hampi Bazaar side is 5.30pm — plan to stay on Hippie Island for dinner or pre-book a private coracle.

eateries.name: Suresh Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Pure-veg Hampi Bazaar workhorse — the lunch stop for domestic pilgrims doing the Virupaksha-Vittala temple circuit. Family-run since the early 1990s, sits 100m from the Virupaksha east gate. North Karnataka jowar-roti thali (sorghum flatbread + brinjal curry + jaggery + dal + buttermilk) is the regional anchor, alongside standard South Indian tiffin. Open 7am-10pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Pre-noon for the jowar thali — it sells out by 1.30pm on weekends. Cash and UPI both work. Avoid the rear courtyard during summer afternoons (40°C+) — the front-room fan tables are cooler.

eateries.name: Mowgli Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Hippie Island staple since the mid-2000s — bamboo-and-thatch huts on the paddy-field edge, set 50m back from the Tungabhadra. Heavy Israeli breakfast skew (shakshuka, labneh, fresh hummus) reflects the long-stay Israeli backpacker corridor that runs Hampi-Pushkar-Manali every winter. Indian thali and momos for lunch crowd. Wi-Fi spotty, electricity load-shedding common 2-5pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Israeli breakfast (9-11am) is the strongest window — shakshuka with brown bread is the order. Closes June-August during monsoon (the dirt path floods). Cash preferred; UPI works when network holds.

eateries.name: Funky Monkey Cafe
eateries.why_it_matters: Anegundi-side cafe (north bank, Kishkindha village) that the Hippie Island crowd cycles to for a day-change. Mango-grove courtyard with paddy-field views; opened mid-2010s as part of the Kishkindha Trust craft-tourism push. Less touristed than Virupapur Gaddi — most patrons are 1-2 day cycle visitors from Hippie Island. Closes during heavy monsoon (Jul-Aug).
eateries.insider_tip: Cycle from Hippie Island via the Tungabhadra north-bank road — 30 min ride past banana plantations and Anjeyanadri Hill base. Combine with the Kishkindha Trust banana-fibre craft workshop next door. Cash only; UPI inconsistent.

stays.name: Goan Corner Guesthouse
stays.why_special: The legendary backpacker guesthouse across the river. Hammocks, rooftop with boulder views, cheap thalis. The social hub of Hampi backpacker scene.

picks.signature_experience: Sunrise and sunset wildlife walks in Yamini Hills; bird watching overlooking the Tungabhadra River; rock-pool immersion pools set among natural boulders.

eateries.name: Hotel Mayura Gerusoppa (KSTDC)
eateries.why_it_matters: The only sit-down restaurant directly at Jog Falls — KSTDC Hotel Mayura Gerusoppa runs the only dining option within walking distance of the British viewpoint. Malnad-style veg meals (₹200) is the lunch order: rice + bisi bele bath + akki rotti (rice-flour flatbread) + jolada rotti + huli (sambar) + chutney + curd. Open 7am-9.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Falls-viewpoint visitors get a 30-40 min lunch crush 12.30-2pm — eat before noon or after 2.30pm for shorter wait. Cards work; UPI works. Closed during monsoon-shutdown weeks if KSTDC schedules maintenance — call ahead +91-8186-244732.

eateries.name: Sharavathi Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Private restaurant at the Jog Falls viewpoint plaza — the alternative to KSTDC Mayura, walk-in friendly with shorter lunch wait. Akki rotti (rice-flour flatbread, a Malnad signature) is the order; the chicken curry meals (₹220) is rice + chicken curry + 2 vegetables + curd. Open 8am-9pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Akki rotti fresh batches every 30 min during lunch — the dough does not hold, so it must be eaten hot. Cash + UPI; cards rare. Closed during peak monsoon weeks (July-Aug) when the viewpoint plaza is wet.
eateries.signature_address: Jog Falls Viewpoint Plaza, Jog Falls 577435

eateries.name: Hotel JP
eateries.why_it_matters: Sagar town main-road institution running 1990s — the gateway-town lunch stop for Jog Falls visitors driving in from Bengaluru/Shimoga. Malnad chicken curry (red chilli + coconut + roasted coriander) on banana leaf is the lunch order; the jolada rotti (sorghum flatbread) with ennegayi (oil-stuffed brinjal curry) is a North Karnataka borrowing on the menu. 30km from Jog. Open 7am-10pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch rush 12.30-2.30pm — KSRTC-bus arrivals from Shimoga fill the room. Akki rotti requires 15 min lead because dough is fresh-mixed per order. Cash + UPI; cards rare.

eateries.name: Hotel Vinayaka
eateries.why_it_matters: Sagar bus-stand pure-veg meals house — the budget default for KSRTC arrivals heading on to Jog. Pure-veg menu, no onion/garlic during the temple-fasting calendar. Veg meals (₹130) is the lunch order; idli-vada-coffee combo (₹70) is breakfast and tiffin. Open 6am-10pm. 30km from Jog.
eateries.insider_tip: Pre-bus 5.30-6.30am for breakfast — fresh idli batch at 6am sharp. Filter coffee here uses Coorg-supplied decoction, distinctly stronger than Bangalore versions. Cash + UPI.

eateries.name: Anand Hotel
eateries.why_it_matters: Sagar Main Road non-veg institution — one of few Malnad-style pork (kadu meenu) restaurants in the Sagar belt. The pork curry uses bone-in country pork + Byadgi chilli + tamarind + coconut paste, a Havyaka-brahmin and Vokkaliga Western Ghats dish that rarely appears on city menus. Country chicken (nati koli) is the alternative. 30km from Jog. Open 11.30am-3.30pm + 7-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Country chicken needs 30 min — call ahead. Pork only Wed-Sun (Mon-Tue meat-shop closed locally). Cash + UPI; cards rare.

eateries.why_it_matters: Waterwoods Lodges is a family-run heritage-style Kabini reservoir resort (since 1988) — restaurant open to non-residents for set lunch and dinner with prior booking. Reservoir-deck seating. ₹1,200-1,700 set menu per person. Open 7am-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch booking 1 day ahead; 8-10 outside-guest covers. The Mangalorean fish curry (the owners are from Mangalore) is a different note from the standard Karnataka-luxury-resort menu. Cards, UPI, cash all work.

eateries.name: JLR Kabini River Lodge Dining
eateries.why_it_matters: JLR Karnataka Kabini River Lodge at Karapur (the original 1986-founded wildlife lodge — the first government-tourism luxury wildlife property in S India) — restaurant open to non-residents for set lunch and dinner with 1-day-advance booking. ₹950-1,400 per person. Open 7am-10pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch booking essential; 6-10 outside-guest covers. The Tuesday Kuruba-cuisine night (₹1,400, tribal-style chicken + foraged greens) is the cultural pull — same kitchen as the Nagarhole-side reservation.

eateries.name: Evolve Back Kuruba Safari Lodge Dining

eateries.insider_tip: Lunch booking 1 day ahead. The Tue/Thu Kuruba-tribal lunch is the cultural pull — bamboo-shoot relish, foraged greens, country-chicken curry. Non-resident pool access ₹800 add-on. Cards, UPI, cash. Resort-casual.

karwar.tagline: Tagore's favourite beach, India's naval base, and the gateway to Devbagh Island

eateries.name: Hotel Amrut
eateries.why_it_matters: Green Street institution running since the 1980s — the Karwar-style fish curry rice (mackerel or surmai in red chilli-coconut gravy with red parboiled rice) is the calling lunch order. The Konkani solar (clams) sukka and crab sukka use Kali estuary catch. Open 11am-3.30pm + 7-10pm year-round.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch 12.30-2pm has the freshest mackerel from the Karwar Old Port morning landing. Ask for "amti rice" (Karwar dal-rice combo) if you skip fish. Cash + UPI; no card terminal.

eateries.name: Anand Lodge
eateries.why_it_matters: College Road lunch-only mainstay running 1990s — the Karwar Konkani fish thali (₹250) is the standard order: red rice + fish curry + fried fish + solar sukka + sol kadhi + papad. Crab xacuti (Goan-influenced) appears on Friday-Sunday. Open 11.30am-3pm + 7-10pm; AC family room.
eateries.insider_tip: Friday Saturday Sunday for crab — limited catch. The sol kadhi (kokum + coconut drink) is house-made and a Konkani digestive default after fish meals. Cash + UPI; cards sometimes.

eateries.name: Roopa Hotel
eateries.why_it_matters: Bus Stand Road pure-veg meals house — the default veg option in a town dominated by Konkani fish kitchens. Udupi-style veg meals (rice + sambar + 2 vegetables + rasam + curd + papad, ₹120) is the lunch order. Open 6.30am-10pm. Pure-veg, no onion/garlic during fasting calendar.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch served 11.30am-3pm; refills unlimited. Filter coffee (Tamil Nadu decoction) ₹20. Cash + UPI; cards rare. Closed second Tuesday monthly.

eateries.name: Hotel Sea Pearl
eateries.why_it_matters: Sit-down seafood restaurant on Tagore Beach Road — the most reliable mid-range Karwari seafood option in town, opened by a Bunt-family operator in the 2010s. Tiger prawns and lobster are the order-ahead premium items; the Karwari fry style (turmeric + chilli + rava crust, no batter) keeps the fish texture intact. Open 12-3.30pm + 7-11pm; AC dining.
eateries.insider_tip: Lobster needs 1 hr lead — call +91-8382-220130. The window tables face Tagore Beach; sundowner 5.30-6.30pm has the best light. Cards + UPI work. Closed Mondays.

eateries.name: Garden Cafe
eateries.why_it_matters: Karwar town cafe running mid-2010s — the only proper coffee-and-cake setup between Gokarna and Karwar, useful for travellers needing wifi + a meal between long bus/car legs. Veg-leaning menu but eggs available. Outdoor garden seating + AC indoor. Open 9am-9.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Morning 9-11am has the freshest baked goods. Wifi password on the table. The mocha is the order; espresso machines are rare in Karwar. Cards + UPI both work.

stays.name: Devbagh Beach Resort

eateries.name: Devaru Bhojanalaya (Temple Prasada Hall)

mangalore.tagline: Coastal Karnataka's capital — Mangalorean cuisine, Kudla culture, and gateway to the Western Ghats

eateries.name: New Taj Mahal Cafe
eateries.signature_dish: Mangalore chicken biryani + gadbad ice cream
eateries.why_it_matters: Hampankatta institution running since 1947 — the default Mangalore biryani address for three generations. Bhatkali-style Nawayath chicken biryani is the calling card, slow-cooked in clay pots with green-chilli paste; the gadbad ice cream cup (layered fruit + jelly + nuts + ice cream) was popularised here in the 1950s. Open 11am-11pm; AC family room upstairs.
eateries.insider_tip: Biryani sells out by 9.30pm — early dinner 7-8pm gets fresh batch. Ask for "kori sukka" (Mangalore dry chicken) as a side. Cash + UPI; cards intermittent. The original Pabba's gadbad recipe came from this kitchen — the family later split with Pabba's Lalbagh going independent.

eateries.name: Pabba's Ideal Ice Cream
eateries.why_it_matters: Mangalore's gadbad ice cream was invented here in the 1970s when Prabhakar Kamath layered leftover ice cream flavours with jelly and fruit on a slow Sunday — the name "gadbad" (Tulu for "mess/confusion") stuck. The Lalbagh ice cream parlour traces its lineage to the 1932 Ideal Cafe; the family runs only this one outlet and explicitly disclaims all Pabba's-branded knock-offs across India. Open 10am-11pm year-round.
eateries.insider_tip: Original gadbad has 9 layers (vanilla + strawberry + butterscotch + chocolate + fresh fruit + jelly + nuts + tutti-frutti + crowning whipped cream) — order "single original" not the family/jumbo size unless splitting. Cash + UPI; no cards. Queues until 10pm in summer; takeaway counter outside has shorter wait.

eateries.name: Hotel Narayana
eateries.signature_dish: Neer dosa with chicken ghee roast
eateries.why_it_matters: Kadri neighbourhood meals house running since the 1980s — the neer dosa (paper-thin rice-flour pancake unique to Tulu Nadu) is the breakfast order, served with chicken ghee roast or coconut chutney. The Mangalorean fish curry meals (₹220) with kane fish + red-chilli gravy + boiled rice is the working-lunch default for Kadri locals. Open 6.30am-10pm year-round.
eateries.insider_tip: Neer dosa fresh batches every 30 min — ask for "thick or thin" (thinner is the traditional Tulu style). The Mangalore buns (sweet banana puris with sambar) at breakfast are a Tulu Sunday-morning staple. Cash + UPI; no card terminal. Closed second Sunday of each month.

eateries.name: Janatha Deluxe
eateries.why_it_matters: Bunder fish-market-side institution — the ghee-roast preparation (Mangalore dry chicken in red Byadgi-chilli + ghee + curry leaves) has been refined here since the 1990s when Janatha popularised it citywide. Pomfret tawa fry uses fish bought 200m away at the morning Bunder auction; crab masala uses backwater crabs from the Netravati. Open 11.30am-3.30pm + 7-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch 12.30-2pm has the freshest fish — Bunder market auctions end at 11am and prep is done by noon. Anjal (seer fish) is the local order; pomfret is the tourist default. Cash + UPI; cards work. Closed Sundays.

eateries.name: Machali
eateries.why_it_matters: Hampankatta sit-down Mangalorean seafood restaurant — the most reliable mid-range option for Bunt and Tuluva coastal cooking in the city, opened mid-2010s by a family from the Bunt restaurant trade. Bangude (mackerel) pulimunchi (tangy chilli) and anjal ghee roast are the orders; the kane (lady-fish) tawa fry is a Tulu monsoon special. Open 12-3.30pm + 7-11pm; AC dining.
eateries.insider_tip: Reserve a window table on the upstairs floor for the Hampankatta street view. Crab and prawn are market-dependent — call ahead (+91-824-2444466). The neer dosa with anjal ghee roast is the textbook Mangalore pairing.

eateries.name: Hotel Mylari
eateries.why_it_matters: Mylari (Nazarbad) is the 1942 origin of the "Mysore Mylari dosa" — softer, thicker, ghee-laden, with potato palya in a deeper-yellow form than the crisp Bengaluru-MTR style. The family-run kitchen has spawned a separate Vinayaka Mylari (1990s split, also on Nazarbad) — locals fight over which is the original. Open 6.30-11am + 4-9pm; closed Mondays.
eateries.insider_tip: Breakfast crush 7-9am; arrive 6.30am for first batch off the tava. ₹70 dosa + ₹25 filter coffee is the standard order. Cash and UPI only; no card. The neighbouring Vinayaka Mylari has near-identical menu — both worth a comparison if you have two breakfasts.

eateries.name: Guru Sweet Mart
eateries.why_it_matters: Guru Sweet Mart on Sayyaji Rao Road is the direct family lineage of Kakasura Madappa — the Mysore Palace chef who is credited with inventing Mysore Pak in 1935 during Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV's reign, using gram flour + ghee + sugar. The original recipe (heavy ghee soak, soft melt) is sold here; modern hard-crunchy versions are at competitor sweet shops. Open 8am-10pm daily.
eateries.insider_tip: Soft Mysore Pak goes stale in 3 days — buy in 250g packs for take-home. The shop also sells boondi laddu and badam halwa; the laddu is a strong second pick. Cash, UPI, card all work. Watch the open-kitchen ghee-pour at 9-10am.

eateries.name: Hotel RRR Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: RRR (Hotel Rama Rao's Restaurant) is a Gandhi Square biryani institution running since the 1970s — donne biryani (palm-leaf cup) is the calling card, Andhra-style heat. The afternoon meals plate (1-2.30pm) draws lawyers and Mysore Palace office staff. Closed first Wednesdays. Open 11am-4pm + 7-10.30pm.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch crush 1-2pm; arrive 12.30 for first donne. Two floors — upstairs AC ₹50 surcharge. Biryani sold by weight (half/full plate). UPI, cash, card all accepted. Vegetarian options minimal.

eateries.name: Vinayaka Bhel House

Family-run since the 1980s. Open 11am-9pm; closed Mondays.

eateries.name: Empire Restaurant Devanahalli
